sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the address page

sections.name: generateStaticParams
sections.title: Listing slugs to build
sections.what: Lists the slug addresses to build when the site is built.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the host create pages in advance for known applications.
sections.watch_out: Slugs added later through the browser are not in this list.

sections.name: ApplicationSlugPage
sections.title: Address page that shows the redirect
sections.what: Reads the slug from the web address and shows the redirect helper with it.
sections.why: Keeps this page small, so the real screen lives in another file.
sections.watch_out: The slug is passed through unchanged, so special characters are not handled here.

summary: The address for one application: it lists known slugs at build time and hands the slug from the web address to a redirect helper.
purpose: Makes web addresses of the form application, slash, slug, lead to the application screen.
why: Likely reason: static hosting needs the full list of addresses at build time, so known slugs are listed ahead of time. The code does not state this.
how: At build time, lists the slugs from the static data file. When a visitor opens a slug address, reads the slug and renders the redirect helper with it.
inputs: The slug from the web address and the applications list from the static data file.
outputs: The redirect helper, which then moves the visitor to the application screen.
risks: Only slugs in the static data file are built ahead of time. Applications created in the browser are not in that list, so they depend on the redirect.
debug: If an application link shows a blank or not-found page, check the slug against the data file. Check that the redirect helper runs.
